cohort: The study included 200 clinically suspected cases of oligohydramnios and polyhydramnios in pregnancies of more than 28 weeks gestational age.
finding: The study identified various predisposing factors and complications associated with oligohydramnios (post term pregnancies, PROM, PIH, chronic abruption placentae) and polyhydramnios (preeclampsia, PROM, preterm labour, abruption placentae, malpresentation, anemia, Rh factor incompatibility, PIH, gestational diabetes mellitus, multifetal gestation).
mod_finding: The proportion of C-section for fetal distress was found to be higher in cases of oligohydramnios.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy (more than 28 weeks gestational age) and at delivery.
